app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:139 — website_name domain match is case-sensitive (no downcasing of website_host/discourse_host), causing benign mismatches but not exploitable disclosure

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:148 — Parent/subdomain match only works when discourse_host is the subdomain of website_host (`discourse_host.ends_with?("."+website_host)`); the reverse case (website is a subdomain of the shorter instance domain, e.g. discourse_host="example.com", website="blog.example.com") falls through to the `else` return of bare host, so the full path is not shown even though the domains share the same organization, an asymmetric/inconsistent same-domain determination

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the “same-site/related-domain” cases that append `URI(website).path` cover (1) exact host match, (2) same-length multi-subdomain hosts with matching base (`www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` when >2 parts), and (3) when the instance host is a subdomain of the website host (`discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`, e.g. `forums.example.com` vs `example.com`). As the finding states, the reverse (`discourse_host="example.com"`, `website_host="blog.example.com"`) is not treated as related and returns only `website_host` (dropping the path). That’s a real, diff-grounded asymmetry/edge-case in the newly added logic, but the diff doesn’t establish that the reverse should be considered “same organization,” so it’s better classified as an incomplete edge case rather than a definite bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:138 — discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname` is used unguarded in `.split('.')` calls; if it ever returns nil/empty (e.g. in test or misconfigured environments) this raises NoMethodError instead of degrading to showing just the website host

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` method assigns `discourse_host = Discourse.current_hostname` and then calls `discourse_host.split('.')` and `discourse_host.ends_with?` without guarding against `nil`/blank. If `current_hostname` were ever `nil` (e.g., misconfiguration), this would raise `NoMethodError`. The diff doesn’t show whether `Discourse.current_hostname` can be nil, so it’s an unhandled edge-case robustness concern rather than a definitively verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:139 — website_name domain match is case-sensitive (no downcasing of website_host/discourse_host), causing benign mismatches but not exploitable disclosure

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the hostname comparisons (`website_host == discourse_host`, the `split('.')` equality checks, and `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`) are all case-sensitive and there is no explicit normalization (e.g., `.downcase`) of either `website_host` or `discourse_host`. This could lead to minor display mismatches if either value is not already normalized, though the diff alone doesn’t prove such inputs occur.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:66 — No test for the reverse parent-domain case (instance domain is a parent of the website domain, e.g. discourse_host=example.com, website_host=forums.example.com), which takes a different path through the same-length/else branches than the tested case

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` (equality, same-length subdomain comparison, and an `ends_with?` parent-domain check). The spec covers: unrelated domains (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`), exact match (`example.com`), and instance as subdomain of website (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com`). It does not cover the reverse case where the instance domain is a parent of the website domain (`Discourse.current_hostname = example.com`, `website_host = forums.example.com`), which would exercise the `else` branch returning `website_host` (not `website_host + path`) and could reveal unintended behavior. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test issue, not a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:66 — No test for same-length multi-label subdomain match branch (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length with length > 2, e.g. www.example.com vs forum.example.com), the trickiest branch in website_name is never exercised

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` logic in `app/serializers/user_serializer.rb` has a distinct branch for same-length, multi-label hosts when `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and `> 2` (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`). The added specs in `spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb` cover: different domain (`discourse.org`), exact same domain (`example.com`), and parent-domain relationship (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com`). None exercise the same-length multi-label subdomain comparison branch, so that nontrivial path is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:66 — No test for single-label discourse_host (e.g. "localhost") where split('.').length > 2 is false, forcing the else/ends_with? branch to be exercised differently

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` logic is already exercised in the spec’s first website_name test (`Discourse.current_hostname` stubbed to `discourse.org`), which takes the same `else` branch as a single-label host like `localhost` (`split('.').length > 2` is false, so it falls through to `ends_with?` and returns `website_host`). The diff does not show any distinct behavior for single-label `discourse_host` that would require separate coverage, so the finding overstates a gap that isn’t meaningfully different from an existing test case.
